cards.0675: A woman in her late seventy-eight empties a bowl with a folded cloth in it under a bath tap and looks at a parcel on the left of her kitchen table that is not fish any more, and the bin lid has not shut since the summer, and a man comes for the bin and tells her a parcel will not go in it and she says nothing about a parcel, and she goes round the side in the afternoon and puts the parcel on the coal in the shed behind the open gate and does not put the padlock on the hasp.
cards.0676: A woman in her late forties is on a fly-tipping job off the ring road with a skip and a skip man and finds a taped parcel with a washed-off label on top of the pile, and her rule is that she does not open other people's things, and she puts it behind the bench in the van with the drawer shut, and she does not go up that road, and her palms are cut and one is dressed and one is not.
cards.0677: A man in his early forties is in a house fitting doors and a woman on the landing asks him about a mark on her ceiling and he does not say what he knows, because saying it would be a visit and a visit takes the gate off somebody, and he looks at a card in his shirt pocket he has carried three weeks and does not ring the number, and he goes back to planing a sill.
cards.0678: A woman in her late seventies goes into her coal shed for coal and the parcel is not on it and there is a clean rectangle in the coal where it sat, and the padlock is still hanging open on the hasp, and she does not go down the road, and she does not ask, and she empties the bowl under the bath tap and the table still stands dead flat.
cards.0679: A woman in her late fifties finds a taped parcel on the low wall of her own garden with a number on the label and the street washed off, and her sister is in the house for the evening, and she brings the parcel in and puts it in the front room under the stool because that is where she does not have to look at things, and she does not go up that road.
cards.0680: A woman in her early thirties has a parcel on the hall table at number ten where the post goes and has had it since Tuesday, and she checks a kitchen calendar and works out twice that Saturday is not a collection day, and puts it out on the step anyway at about eleven, and it rains on it, and she brings it back in on the back mat, and her back door shuts true over it.
cards.0681: A woman in her late forties has the parcel behind the bench in the van where it has been and takes a job where a woman cannot put one thing in the skip, and she does not open the parcel, and she drives past the end of that road and does not turn in, and the drawer under the bench is shut with the bolster in it and there is still no invoice for four hours in August.
cards.0682: A man in his early forties shuts the open drawer at half six and thinks about it an hour later at the lights, and buys oak from a woman at the till who asks him to tell his sister Friday is not a date, and is at a merchant tip in the afternoon and finds a taped parcel with a number and a street he has driven past, reads the name, puts it back down the way it was, does not put it in his van, writes TWELVE on a scrap of scribing card into his shirt pocket, and tapes a folded bag over its top corner.
cards.0683: A woman in her late seventies finds a lad she has never spoken to putting a taped parcel on the grass inside her open gate without knocking, and she brings it in and puts it on the left of her own kitchen table where it has been since the twelfth of October, and the envelope stays square with the edge on the right of it.
cards.0684: A woman in her late seventies has the parcel on the left of her table and a woman with a bright voice comes up the path on the date a machine gave her in October and asks about water staining and says it is for the freeholder and not for you, and the door is not on the latch, and she is let in, and the surveyor asks what the box is and what is in it and whether it was opened and she tells her the truth out loud, and the surveyor goes up for twenty-five minutes and comes back down and hands her a second printed card with the same free number on it, and both cards go in the apron pocket with the two drop bolts, and she has rung neither.
